messages.text: I’ll trace how progress is subscribed and delivered, then update the panel path and run the workspace’s visible checks.

The panel helper starts the feed before adding its listener, so it misses a synchronous cached packet. I’ll subscribe before startup and order decoded frames by packet arrival; progress history will still receive every accepted frame.

The first check found a mistaken test assumption: an already subscribed telemetry listener receives a later panel startup event. That matches the shared feed’s existing behavior. I’ll verify telemetry’s own startup separately and continue checking cleanup and delayed decoding.

Restored the initial panel update by subscribing before the progress feed starts. Decoded frames now paint in packet arrival order, so a late older frame cannot roll the display backward. Accepted frames still enter progress history, and cancellation prevents later packets from reaching a released attempt.

The visible Node checks passed for warm startup, streaming, reversed decode completion, retry, hide, reuse, telemetry, queue record shape, and synchronous reentry. `git diff --check` was unavailable because this workspace is not a Git repository.
